headline: Mystery of Mars' Doomed Moon Phobos May Finally Be Solved
meta_description: Scientists studying a giant crater on Mars' moon Phobos believe they may finally solve the riddle of where the doomed moon came from.
summary_short: A massive crater on Phobos could hold the key to understanding whether Mars' innermost moon is a captured asteroid or formed from ancient debris.
body:
A giant crater on Mars' innermost moon, Phobos, may finally unlock a decades-old mystery: where did this small, irregularly shaped world come from? Researchers presenting work at the European Geosciences Union assembly in Vienna have modeled how the enormous Stickney Crater—measuring 9 kilometers across—could reveal the moon's internal structure and, with it, its origin. Scientists believe Phobos either began as an asteroid captured by Mars' gravity, or formed from debris hurled into orbit after a massive object struck Mars roughly 4.2 billion years ago. By mapping Phobos' gravity field in greater detail, particularly around Stickney Crater, researchers hope to detect whether the impact created a denser region of compressed material beneath the surface—a signature that could definitively answer the question.

Phobos orbits Mars once every 7 hours and 39 minutes, racing closer to the planet with each passing year. Despite its small mean diameter of only 22.2 kilometers, this moon has proven remarkably resilient. An impact large enough to carve out Stickney Crater should have shattered such a small body, unless Phobos possesses an unusually low and uniform density—much like a sponge capable of absorbing the blow. The intense heat from that collision would have melted and compressed stone beneath the crater, potentially leaving traces scientists can measure.

Japan's upcoming MMX sample return mission promises to provide the detailed measurements and physical evidence needed to solve this puzzle. Current estimates suggest Phobos has a porous interior possibly containing water ice, with denser material concentrated near its equatorial region. As Phobos spirals slowly toward Mars—destined eventually to break apart or collide with the planet—this preserved record of events billions of years old offers a rare window into the early solar system.
quick_facts: Stickney Crater is 9 kilometers in diameter on Phobos
Phobos orbits Mars once every 7 hours and 39 minutes
The moon has a mean diameter of only 22.2 kilometers
Scientists presented research at the Vienna geosciences assembly
Japan's MMX mission will provide crucial sample evidence
